shortDescription: Shares of Mexican logistics and transportation company Traxion BMV:TRAXION/A  jumped on Tuesday after a company linked to its co-founder Aby Lijtszain announced plans to launch a voluntary tender offer for up to 100% of the company's outstanding shares.

children: Shares of Mexican logistics and transportation company Traxion
jumped on Tuesday after a company linked to its co-founder Aby Lijtszain announced plans to launch a voluntary tender offer for up to 100% of the company's outstanding shares.
Traxion shares closed up 13.9% at 12.41 pesos on Tuesday, below the proposed offer price of 13.18 pesos per share.
According to exchange filings, the proposed tender offer would cover Traxion's 542.4 million outstanding shares.
The offer price represents a premium of more than 20% to Traxion's average share price over the 60 trading days ended September 11, the company said.

Lijtszain founded passenger transportation company LIPU before co-founding Traxión in 2011. The company provides freight transportation, logistics and passenger mobility services in Mexico through 12 operating brands and serves more than 1,300 customers.
Brokerage Actinver said the proposed offer price implies upside from Traxion's September 14 closing price, although it remains below the firm's 12-month target price of 14.50 pesos.
The company said on Tuesday the prospective bidder had confirmed the tender offer is not intended to delist the company or cancel the registration of its shares.
